show sunday
scene makidrive1
: Sensei?...
: I’m sorry to wake you up so early, but...
: There’s a stranger in our house.
scene black
: I’m going back to sleep.
: You’re going to leave me to die just like that?!
scene makidrive2
: Ami, if there was an actual stranger in our house, I know for a fact you wouldn’t be calmly discussing it with me after gently waking me up.
: Okay...So maybe it isn’t a stranger per se, but it’s still someone who shouldn’t be here!
: Then tell them to go home. I’m tired.
: I tried! But she walked right past me and poured herself a cup of coffee that I made for you and then sat down on the couch like she owned the place!
: Ugh...who is it then? Noriko? Ayane?
: It’s that frickin’ lube dealer again! And she didn’t even bring any samples this time!
Maki?
She’s here?
: If it’s her...I’ll be up in a second. I just need to get dressed.
scene makidrive3
: What do you mean, “If it’s her?” How the heck am I supposed to interpret that?
: You can interpret it by making more coffee since Maki has apparently taken mine.
scene makidrive4
: Fine! But only because I love you and would do whatever you tell me, no matter what it is.
: I’m aware. Thanks, Ami.
scene black
Ami leaves the room and I bring myself to my feet, throwing on the shirt Molly made for me- a shirt that was neatly folded by my “beloved” niece and placed on my desk sometime this morning.
If Maki’s here, it can really only mean one of two things.
Either the conversation she had with Sara yesterday dramatically failed and she has nowhere else to turn to-
Or it didn’t fail. And she just needs my help with Makoto again because she can’t figure out how to believe in herself as a parent.
I’m not sure why that would cause her to believe in me, a significantly worse “parent,” but if she’s already here, I shouldn’t keep her waiting.
Especially since every second I spend not supervising Ami when she’s near her increases Maki’s chance of being poisoned.
scene makidrive5
: Morning. Do you always sleep this late?
: It’s like 8:00 AM.
: I know. I just figured I’d try making a joke that isn’t depressing, dark, or sexual. Which is probably why it didn’t come out very funny.
: While I admire the effort, I would like to know what you’re doing here.
: Not even going to try waking up first? Just gonna jump straight to business?
: Sit down. Have a cup of coffee. Take your time. I’m in no rush.
scene makidrive6
: You drank his coffee. Now I have to brew more since somebody doesn’t have any manners.
: While you’re at it, would you mind making some more for me as well? I’ve been up since 4:00 AM, so I can kind of use it.
: Would you like me to add a little something to it that will help you sleep better tonight? Much better?
Okay. So, apparently supervising Ami won’t stop her from trying to poison Maki either. That’s...good to know.
: Ami, don’t poison our house guests please.
scene makidrive7
: You never let me do anything fun anymore!
: Thanks for looking out for me. I roofied myself once just to see what it was like and, honestly? It’s not really all it's cracked up to be.
: I...don’t think that’s a thing people really “crack up” to be all that exciting.
scene makidrive8
Ami returns to the kitchen, giving me an opportunity to press a little further about Maki’s reason for coming.
: Want to go for a drive?
But before I can even ask, she opens her mouth and says that.
: Depends. Are you so deeply distressed that you’re going to drive us off a cliff?
: No. But I will drive at least 20 mph over the speed limit and make plenty of rolling stops.
: You’re lucky Kumon-mi uses American measurement systems or I wouldn’t even know how fast that is.
: And you’re lucky that the roads aren’t busy this early in the morning. Rolling stops are dangerous.
scene makidrive9
: Especially when-
: Talk about something else.
scene makidrive10
: Hm? Did I miss something?
: No.
scene makidrive11
: Got it.
: Anyway, as I was saying, you’re coming with me. I’ve got a little bit of a problem I could use your help with.
: Does that problem wear glasses and get straight A’s?
: Usually. Right now? Not really.
: Does this have something to do with Makoto getting called to the office the other day?
: Because if she’s been starting trouble, I don’t know if I’ll feel safe in class anymore.
: As the class president, she should be-
: Knock it off, Ami.
scene makidrive12
: I was only kidding this time!
: Makoto’s fine. We’re just having some family problems right now.
scene makidrive13
: Family problems?...
: It’s nothing you need to worry about.
: Ami?
scene makidrive14
: Oh! Umm...
: Coffee!
: I’ll...be right back.
scene black
Strangely enough, Ami retreats to her room without being told after bringing the two of us a fresh pot of coffee.
I guess saying “strangely enough” is a little...dismissive, though. Especially when it’s likely that she’s in the early stages of putting two and two together.
But while I wish I could stick around and see firsthand just what that dramatic realization does to her, I have been given a job.

I am not sure if it is a job that I can handle...nor a job I even want, but Maki’s assertion (Combined with her exceedingly flattering soccer mom getup) forces me to come along regardless of what I want.
And before I know it, I find myself in the passenger seat of a car- checking three times to make sure my seatbelt is buckled.
scene makidrive15
: Are you nervous?
: About what? Seeing Makoto?
: About anything. You’ve been biting your nails and staring out of the window ever since I started the car.
: My driving isn’t that bad, is it?
: Your driving’s fine. I didn’t even realize I was acting strangely.
: I don’t know. Maybe I am nervous about seeing Makoto. But it would be a more...subconscious thing than me actively going over it in my head.
: Cheering people up isn’t really one of my specialties.
: Yeah, that’s one of many things we have in common. And probably the most boring and depressing out of all of them as well.
: So, how is she doing exactly? And...better question, what do you want me to do about it?

: I’m pretty sure she hasn’t left her room since I took her home on Friday. But I was out for a good portion of the day yesterday, so I guess it’s possible she got up to use the bathroom or something.
: I really hope so.
: I’m surprised you felt comfortable leaving her, though. I figured you’d be attached at the hip right now.
: To be completely honest, I’m pretty sure that would just make things worse for her.
: Miku’s been staying over, though. And at least Makoto doesn’t try to keep her away.
: I dropped her off back at the dorm this morning. Poor girl’s gotten less sleep than both of us.
if kirinkill == False:
: Yeah, well...
: I think we both probably know why.
scene makidrive16
: I mean...I know why. Do you know why?
: I know enough about her past to piece it together. I just don’t really know the specifics.
scene makidrive15
: Huh.
: You two are closer than I thought.
: Miku doesn’t normally share that with people she doesn’t completely trust.
: To be fair, I didn’t exactly learn it from her.
: At the risk of harboring a vendetta against whoever told you, I’m going to suggest that we cut this conversation short and just...leave it at our mutual understanding of Miku’s sadness.
: That girl’s been through enough. Talking about this without her knowing just doesn’t sit right with me.
: Fair enough. I wasn’t trying to get the details out of you or anything.
: If Miku trusts you, she’ll tell you. That’s really all you need to know.
else:
: She really cares about Makoto, doesn’t she?
: Yeah...
: Yeah, she does.
Maki goes back to focusing on the road as a long and uncomfortable silence emerges from the backseat of her car and crawls its way onto the center console.
In this abrupt, unwelcome separation comes the realization that I am biting off much more than I can chew right now.
That realization grows and festers with every passing stoplight, infecting my body and liquefying my teeth to the point where I can no longer bite anything.
It doesn’t make a difference whether or not Maki intends to drive us off a cliff when I started falling to my death the moment I checked my seatbelt for the third time.
I want this car to turn around.
I want the suffering to end without my intervention- because if there is anything I have learned over my time here, it is that the past repeats itself.
And that if my ways of handling Makoto were even the slightest bit successful, I wouldn’t have to keep fixing her.
: You’re doing it again.
: Doing what?
: Biting your nails.
: You should stop. It’s gross.
scene black
Maki continues driving, twenty miles per hour over the speed limit on almost every street we take.
But she stops at every stop sign.
scene makidrive17
: So, uhh...do you mind if I get mildly sappy for a minute or two before I take you up to see Makoto?
: Take as long as you like because I still have no idea what I’m going to say to her.
: I mean...I don’t think you really need to say anything. It’s not like I expect you to go up there and be like, “Hey, Makoto. Sorry your dad’s dead. Feel better now.”
: She just...
: I don’t know. I keep wanting to say this is something I should be able to handle on my own, but...the more I think about it, the more I realize that might be the exact problem.
: Makoto can’t see me without also seeing her father. And it’s that constant reminder that I think is making this so hard for her.
: So...serious question. Do you think she can see me without seeing her father?
scene makidrive18
: I think...
: Okay. So, you’re obviously the only male authority figure left in her life now. And one that she admires greatly.
: But even with that, I don’t think she’ll ever see you as anything more than her teacher or...maybe a schoolgirl crush.
I think it’s a lot more than just a crush at this point...
: That girl just...does better with people like you than people like me. It’s a respect thing.
: Like, how is she going to be consoled by someone she automatically associates sex jokes and dildos with?
: Each time I try to hold her hand, she’s probably thinking “Wow, this hand has touched so many sex toys.”
: I haven’t seen Makoto since Friday, but I’m pretty sure that is not what she’d be thinking.
scene makidrive19
: I don’t know what she’d be thinking, though. I never know what she’s thinking because her brain is on another level than mine.
: She’s stubborn. She needs someone on the same level as her to talk to or she’s just going to keep circling the drain.
: With all due respect, I think Makoto is several levels above me as well.
: She might be. But I don’t think she sees it that way.
: To her, you’re a role model. Someone she aspires to be. Someone she’ll actually listen to because you’re not just a joke to her.
: You’re not me.
scene makidrive20
: Oh, and if you’re having second thoughts about this, I’m not giving you a ride home. I am out of other options and turning to you is pretty much my last ditch effort.
: Have you considered time?
scene makidrive21
: Well, obviously! But time alone doesn’t cure anything when it feels like the walls are closing in around you.
: I need her to feel safe. I need someone to stop those walls from closing in and I’m not strong enough to hold them back on my own.
: For what it’s worth, I think you are. But fuck it. I’ll give it a shot.
: If this doesn’t work though and your daughter just winds up becoming even worse due to something I said, you owe me free porn forever.
: That’s so much porn!
: Yes. I have a problem.
: Okay, fine. But don’t go screwing this up on purpose just to fuel your addiction.
So either Makoto cheers up or I get free porn forever. At least I can’t lose anymore.
: Deal. Pleasure doing business with you.
: Maybe I’ll even throw in an added bonus of trying to cheer you up if whatever methods I use on Makoto actually work.
scene makidrive22
: Oh, come on...You don’t have to worry about me.
: I’ve got two close friends who can cheer me up when I need it. You’re here for my daughter.
: I am. But I’m here because you brought me. Which means that you deserve something too.
scene makidrive23
: Then I’d like to sacrifice my reward for an additional serving of Makoto’s happiness.
: You know...you’re a pretty great mom for someone who thinks they’re a pretty shitty mom.
: Tell me that again when I don’t feel pressured to rely on a third party to console my daughter because I suck at it.
: And then again when I stop being creeped out by how off she looks when she’s grieving.
Wait...
scene makotoflashback
: Until everything melts down and reforms into one disturbing mass of flesh, complete with twelve smiles.
: One for each girl in class that you [masturbate] to while all alone in bed at night.
scene makidrive23
Oh no.
: Uhh...
: Welp! Time to go. Makoto’s not going to cheer herself up.
: On second thought, maybe I’ll-
scene black
: Nope! No more procrastinating. We’ve talked for long enough.
: But what if I’m also creeped out by her?
: You’re like three times her size. What do you possibly have to be afraid of?
: You sell whips. What do you have to be afraid of?
: Are you suggesting that I whip my daughter? I’m into some weird shit, Sensei, but that’s just crossing a line.
: Hah...
Maki leads me up a dark staircase, but it’s not dark enough to conceal the array of framed photos hanging on her wall.
They’ve all been turned backwards.
